idea: Faceless illustrated mini-documentaries on the hidden engineering, design decisions and strange history of everyday things (The Curious Mechanism playbook).
audience: Global, English-speaking, 18-44, curious adults who watch engineering, design and history explainers
promise: one everyday object, one question, the hidden engineering behind it
notes: Source: the-curious-mechanism.zip playbook (PLAYBOOK.md, brand/style-guide.md). Niche leaders (Half as Interesting, Practical Engineering, Jared Owen, Steve Mould, Primal Space) share: a question-title (Why/How), a 15-20 s hook with no intro, one clean diagram look, 8-15 min long-form plus Shorts cut from it. Gap: none uses a 19th-century engraving / patent-drawing look; that is the brand. Long-form 8-12 min weekly on YouTube; 2-3 Shorts a week (30-55 s, 9:16, complete mini-story) on every platform. Brand font is Libre Baskerville (Google Fonts); kit uses DejaVu Serif because kit.py renders with locally installed fonts. Handle 'curiousmechanism' is 16 chars, over the 15-char X limit, so handles are shortened. 2026-11-13: look changed from the playbook's engraving to a clean 2D cartoon (engraving was faded on phones; cartoon picked over cinematic painted after a side-by-side test); stories open on what went wrong.

names.why: Playbook name kept; ai suffix says AI-made up front; 13 chars fits X.
Closest to the full name; 14 chars; AI disclosure stays in the bio.
Shortest, easiest to spell after hearing it once.

style.look: Clean 2D cartoon illustration, like a high-quality animated educational series: bold clean outlines, flat colours with soft cel shading, simple readable shapes, expressive characters with large clear faces and simple features. Period-accurate clothes, aircraft and rooms for the year in the scene, simplified but correct. Strong contrast and a limited palette of deep teal, warm amber, cream and a bright red for danger or the key part. The subject is large and fills the frame. People are anonymous, friendly and ordinary, with clear emotion.
style.avatar_subject: a single brass gear drawn as a clean 2D cartoon icon, bold outline, warm amber on a deep teal background, centered, no text
style.banner_scene: a wide clean 2D cartoon scene at dusk: a 1950s jet airliner high over the sea in the centre band, warm amber light on its silver skin, calm dark teal sky towards the edges
style.banner_line: the hidden engineering of everyday things

youtube.name: The Curious Mechanism
youtube.description:
Welcome to The Curious Mechanism.

Every video answers one question about an everyday thing: why airplane windows are round, what is inside a ballpoint pen, how GPS knows where you are. We look at the hidden engineering, the design decisions and the strange history behind ordinary objects.

How it's made: every topic is researched from at least two reliable sources, listed in each description. Illustrations and narration are made with AI tools; research, script and editing are done by a person.

A new mini-documentary every week, Shorts in between.

Nothing is ordinary when you understand how it works. Tell us in the comments which everyday object we should open up next.
